name: Canva
description: Let your AI work in Canva: find and read designs, create new ones, export them to PDF, PNG, PowerPoint or video with download links, organise folders, upload images from a link, read brand templates and comment on designs.
instructions:
## Canva
This connector works with a Canva account through the **Canva REST API** (formerly Connect API, `https://api.canva.com/rest/v1`), as the user who authorizes it: designs (list, search, read, create), exports to PDF, PNG, JPG, PPTX, MP4 and more with download links, folders, uploaded assets (read, rename, upload from a URL), brand templates and comments.

**Setup (one-time, about 10 minutes)**
1. Turn on multi-factor authentication for your Canva account (Canva requires it for developers): Settings → Login & security.
2. Open the Canva Developer Portal at https://www.canva.com/developers/apps, click **Create an app** and pick who it is for. A **private** app (only possible on a Canva Enterprise team) is approved by your own team admins; a **public** app works for its developer and needs Canva's review before other Canva users can authorize it. Then open **Outside Canva → Start integrating**.
3. Under **Configuration → Scopes** tick: `profile:read`, `design:meta:read`, `design:content:read`, `design:content:write`, `folder:read`, `folder:write`, `asset:read`, `asset:write`, `brandtemplate:meta:read`, `brandtemplate:content:read`, `comment:read`, `comment:write`. The connector asks for all of them; Canva refuses an authorization that asks for a scope not ticked here.
4. Under **Authentication** add the redirect URL `https://cloud.anythingmcp.com/api/mcp-oauth/callback` on AnythingMCP Cloud, or `<your AnythingMCP URL>/api/mcp-oauth/callback` when you host AnythingMCP yourself. For a local test Canva accepts `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/...`, not `localhost`.
5. Copy the **Client ID** and generate a **Client secret** (shown only once) into `CANVA_CLIENT_ID` and `CANVA_CLIENT_SECRET`, install the connector, click **Authorize with Provider** and allow access in Canva. Access tokens last about four hours and are renewed automatically; each refresh token works once and is replaced on every renewal.

**Smaller scope set**: to keep the connector read-only, untick the `:write` scopes in the portal and in the connector's OAuth settings, authorize again and switch off the tools that create, change or move things.

**Exports** run as jobs: `canva_create_export` returns a job id, then call `canva_get_export` every few seconds until `status` is `success`; `urls` holds one link per file, valid 24 hours. Check the possible formats first with `canva_get_design_export_formats`. Designs with premium elements the user has not licensed fail with `license_required`. Limits: 75 exports per user per 5 minutes and 500 per day.

**Uploads from a URL** run as jobs too: `canva_upload_asset_from_url`, then `canva_get_asset_upload` until `success`.

**Folders**: `root` stands for the top level of the user's Projects and `uploads` for the Uploads folder (`canva_list_folder_items`, `canva_create_folder`, `canva_move_folder_item`).

**Plans**: designs, folders, assets, exports and comments work on every plan, including free. Brand templates need a plan with brand templates (Pro, Teams or Enterprise); `canva_get_capabilities` shows `brand_template` when it is available.

**Preview APIs**: comments and uploads from a URL are Canva preview APIs; they can change without notice, and a public app using them cannot pass Canva's review. For a public app, switch off `canva_upload_asset_from_url`, `canva_get_asset_upload` and the comment tools.

**Confirm first**: `canva_create_comment` and `canva_reply_to_comment` are seen by collaborators. `canva_delete_folder` and `canva_delete_asset` (move to Trash) are installed switched off.

**Ids**: a design id is the part after `/design/` in a Canva link (`https://www.canva.com/design/DAFVztcvd9z/...`). Thumbnail URLs expire after 15 minutes, `edit_url` and `view_url` after 30 days. Times are Unix seconds.

**Common errors** (`code` in the answer)
- `invalid_access_token`, `revoked_access_token`: authorize again.
- `missing_scope`: tick the scope in the portal and in the connector's OAuth settings, then authorize again.
- `permission_denied`, `not_found` (`design_not_found`, `folder_not_found`, `asset_not_found`): the user cannot see that object or the id is wrong.
- 403 "requires one of capabilities": a paid feature such as brand templates.
- `too_many_requests`: most calls allow 10 to 100 per minute per user; wait a minute.

**Out of scope here**: editing design content, autofill, resizing, imports of files, AI generation, design analytics and webhooks.

CANVA_CLIENT_ID.label: Client ID
CANVA_CLIENT_ID.help: Canva Developer Portal → your app → Outside Canva → Configuration: Client ID.
CANVA_CLIENT_ID.patternMessage: Paste the Client ID without spaces.

CANVA_CLIENT_SECRET.label: Client secret
CANVA_CLIENT_SECRET.help: Same page → Generate secret. Shown only once.
CANVA_CLIENT_SECRET.patternMessage: Paste the client secret without spaces.

verifyHints.401: Canva refused the access token. Click Authorize with Provider again; if the client secret was regenerated, update CANVA_CLIENT_SECRET first.
verifyHints.403: The authorization lacks a scope (missing_scope) or the user cannot use this feature. Tick the scopes in the Canva Developer Portal, then authorize again.
verifyHints.rate_limited: Canva is rate limiting this user. Wait a minute and try again.

prerequisites: A Canva account with multi-factor authentication turned on and an app in the Canva Developer Portal with the redirect URL below and the scopes listed in the setup. A private app needs Canva Enterprise; a public one works for its developer before review. About 10 minutes.

authConfig.scopes: profile:read design:meta:read design:content:read design:content:write folder:read folder:write asset:read asset:write brandtemplate:meta:read brandtemplate:content:read comment:read comment:write

tools.name: canva_get_me
tools.description: Read who authorized the connector: the Canva user_id and team_id. Needs no scope; a quick check that the authorization works.

tools.name: canva_get_profile
tools.description: Read the display name of the signed-in Canva user (scope profile:read).

tools.name: canva_get_capabilities
tools.description: List the paid features the signed-in user can use through the API, e.g. brand_template, autofill, resize, export_png_transparency. An empty list means a free plan: brand templates are then not available (scope profile:read).

tools.name: canva_list_designs
tools.description: List or search the user's designs, with id, title, owner, page_count, a thumbnail (its URL expires after 15 minutes), edit_url and view_url (valid 30 days, open them only as the user) and created_at and updated_at as Unix seconds. The answer has items[] and, when there are more, continuation (scope design:meta:read).

ownership.description: Whose designs: any (default), owned or shared.

continuation.description: The continuation token of the previous answer, for the next page.

tools.name: canva_get_design
tools.description: Read one design by id: title, owner, page_count, thumbnail, edit_url, view_url and timestamps (scope design:meta:read). The design id is the part after /design/ in a Canva link, e.g. DAFVztcvd9z.

tools.name: canva_create_design
tools.description: Create a new, empty design and return it with id, edit_url and view_url (scope design:content:write). design_type is either a preset, {"type": "preset", "name": "presentation"} (doc, email, presentation or whiteboard), or a custom size in pixels, {"type": "custom", "width": 1080, "height": 1080} (40 to 8000 each). asset_id optionally places an image asset on it. The design opens in the user's Projects.

title.description: Title of the design, 1 to 255 characters.

asset_id.description: Id of an image asset to put on the design.

tools.name: canva_get_design_export_formats
tools.description: List the file formats a design can be exported to (pdf, jpg, png, svg, pptx, gif, mp4, html_bundle, html_standalone, csv), depending on its type. Check it before canva_create_export (scope design:content:read).

tools.name: canva_create_export
tools.description: Start exporting a design to a file. format is an object with type and options, e.g. {"type": "pdf", "size": "a4"}, {"type": "png", "width": 1080, "pages": [1]}, {"type": "jpg", "quality": 80} (quality is required for jpg), {"type": "pptx"} or {"type": "mp4", "quality": "horizontal_1080p"}. Returns job.id with status in_progress: read it with canva_get_export until status is success, which carries the download URLs. Limited to 75 exports per 5 minutes per user (scope design:content:read).

format.description: Export format with type (pdf, jpg, png, gif, pptx, mp4, html_bundle, html_standalone, csv) and its options: pages (page numbers from 1), export_quality (regular or pro), size for pdf (a4, a3, letter, legal), width and height for images, quality for jpg (1 to 100) and mp4, lossless, transparent_background and as_single_image for png.

tools.name: canva_get_export
tools.description: Read an export job: status (in_progress, success or failed), and on success urls[], one download link per file (multi-page images give one per page; links expire after 24 hours). A failed job explains why in error.code, e.g. license_required for premium elements (scope design:content:read).

export_id.description: The job id returned by canva_create_export.

tools.name: canva_list_folder_items
tools.description: List what a folder contains, with each item's type (design, folder, image, brand_template) and details. Use root for the top level of the user's Projects and uploads for the Uploads folder. Videos are not listed; brand templates only when item_types names them. The answer has items[] and continuation (scope folder:read).

folder_id.description: The folder id, or root for the top level of Projects, or uploads.

item_types.description: Comma-separated item types, e.g. design,folder (default: design, folder and image).

continuation.description: The continuation token of the previous answer, for the next page.

tools.name: canva_get_folder
tools.description: Read a folder by id: name, thumbnail and timestamps (scope folder:read). root and uploads are aliases, not folders, and cannot be read here.

tools.name: canva_create_folder
tools.description: Create a folder in the user's Projects (parent_folder_id root), in Uploads (uploads) or inside another folder. Returns the folder with its id (scope folder:write).

parent_folder_id.description: Where to create it: root, uploads or a folder id.

tools.name: canva_rename_folder
tools.description: Rename a folder; the name is the only thing that can be changed (scope folder:write).

tools.name: canva_move_folder_item
tools.description: Move a design, folder or image into another folder (to_folder_id root for the top level of Projects). Fails with item_in_multiple_folders when the item sits in more than one folder (scope folder:write).

item_id.description: Id of the design, folder or image asset to move.

tools.name: canva_delete_folder
tools.description: Delete a folder. The user's own designs and files in it move to the Trash; items owned by others go back to their owner's Projects. Installed switched off; confirm with the user first (scope folder:write).

tools.name: canva_get_asset
tools.description: Read an uploaded asset (image or video): name, tags, owner, thumbnail and timestamps (scope asset:read).

tools.name: canva_update_asset
tools.description: Rename an asset or replace its tags. tags replaces the whole list (up to 50 tags) (scope asset:write).

tags.description: The complete new list of tags.

tools.name: canva_delete_asset
tools.description: Move an asset to the Trash. Designs that already use it keep it. Installed switched off; confirm with the user first (scope asset:write).

tools.name: canva_upload_asset_from_url
tools.description: Start uploading an image or video from a public URL into the user's Uploads. Returns job.id with status in_progress; read it with canva_get_asset_upload until status is success, which carries the new asset and its id (scope asset:write). This is a Canva preview API: it can change without notice.

name.description: Name of the asset, up to 50 characters.

url.description: Public https URL of the file, up to 2048 characters.

tools.name: canva_get_asset_upload
tools.description: Read an upload job started with canva_upload_asset_from_url: status in_progress, success (with asset and its id) or failed (error.code file_too_big, import_failed or fetch_failed) (scope asset:read). This is a Canva preview API: it can change without notice.

job_id.description: The job id returned by canva_upload_asset_from_url.

tools.name: canva_list_brand_templates
tools.description: List the brand templates the user can use, with id, title, view_url, create_url and thumbnail. Needs a Canva plan with brand templates (Pro, Teams or Enterprise; canva_get_capabilities shows brand_template) and scope brandtemplate:meta:read. items is empty when there are none.

ownership.description: Whose templates: any (default), owned or shared.

dataset.description: non_empty for only templates with autofill fields (default any).

continuation.description: The continuation token of the previous answer, for the next page.

tools.name: canva_get_brand_template
tools.description: Read one brand template by id: title, view_url, create_url (opens a new design from it), thumbnail and timestamps (scope brandtemplate:meta:read, plan with brand templates).

tools.name: canva_get_brand_template_dataset
tools.description: Read the autofill fields of a brand template: each field name with its type (text, image or chart). Shows what data the template expects (scope brandtemplate:content:read, plan with brand templates).

tools.name: canva_create_comment
tools.description: Start a comment thread on a design, optionally assigned to a collaborator. Collaborators see it and may be notified, so confirm the text with the user. Returns the thread with its id (scope comment:write). This is a Canva preview API: it can change without notice.

message_plaintext.description: The comment, up to 2048 characters. Mention a user as [user_id:team_id].

assignee_id.description: User id to assign the comment to; must be mentioned in the message.

tools.name: canva_get_comment_thread
tools.description: Read a comment thread on a design: the comment, its author, assignee, resolution state and timestamps. Canva has no call that lists all threads of a design, so the thread id must be known (scope comment:read). This is a Canva preview API: it can change without notice.

tools.name: canva_list_comment_replies
tools.description: List the replies in a comment thread, oldest first, with author and text. The answer has items[] and continuation (scope comment:read). This is a Canva preview API: it can change without notice.

continuation.description: The continuation token of the previous answer.

tools.name: canva_reply_to_comment
tools.description: Reply to a comment thread on a design (up to 100 replies per thread). Collaborators see it, so confirm the text with the user (scope comment:write). This is a Canva preview API: it can change without notice.
